shape.basis: Wesson et al. (2024, Sect. 5.5): molecular hydrogen dominates three of this picture's four filters (2.12, 3.0 and 3.35 µm); the fourth, 1.62 µm, is continuum and hydrogen recombination lines of the ionised gas. Kastner et al. (2025, Sect. IV) match their SMA CO(2-1) cube with a thin expanding ellipsoidal shell of molecular gas around the ionised gas, whose form the near-infrared H2 pictures share: axial ratios 1.0 : 0.71 : 0.82, 1.1e+18 cm by 7.6e+17 cm on the sky at 782 pc (semi-axes 47 and 32.5 arcsec), turned to position angle about 70 degrees and viewed within about 2 degrees of its third axis, expanding at 30 km/s along its longest axis: 0.6383 km/s per arcsec, and 24.6 km/s along the sight line. The red and green channels, molecular hydrogen, take that speed. The blue channel, with the ionised gas's light, takes the Main Ring's [N II] speed, 19 km/s (O'Dell et al. 2013, Sect. III.3): a choice made here. The shell is open at both poles; the opening is modelled there by an elongated ellipsoid of radius 2.3e+17 cm, 19.7 arcsec. Through it the picture shows the ionised gas of the central cavity (Wesson et al., Sect. 4.1), which takes the Lobes' [O III] speed, 28 km/s, in every channel (O'Dell et al. 2013): a choice made here, the middle of the three speeds that paper gives the Lobes. The shell's tilt of about 2 degrees has no printed direction and is not applied. The smooth light is read over 16 face pixels, a presentation value.
